full_text_en:
Zhenjiang Hongxing Magnetic Separation Equipment Co., Ltd. v. Zhenjiang Housing Provident Fund Management Center and Gu Zhangze — Dispute over Revocation of an Administrative Handling Decision

Ruling Summary

Housing provident funds are long-term housing savings that units and their employees must contribute to in accordance with the law, and their contribution is compulsory and exclusive. The "Regulations on the Administration of Housing Provident Funds" specify the scope, subjects, amounts, methods, time limits for contributions, as well as the withdrawal, use, management, and supervision of housing provident funds. The state implements a compulsory savings and dedicated account storage system for housing provident funds. Units shall contribute housing provident funds for their employees in a timely manner in accordance with the statutory methods and amounts, and may not change the contribution method or reduce the contribution obligation through negotiation.

Plaintiff: Zhenjiang Hongxing Magnetic Separation Equipment Co., Ltd., domiciled at Nangang Group, West side of Runxing Road, Zhenjiang City, Jiangsu Province.
Legal Representative: Tang Hong, General Manager of the company.

Defendant: Zhenjiang Housing Provident Fund Management Center, Jiangsu Province, domiciled at Nanshan Road, Zhenjiang City.
Legal Representative: Zhang Yueming, Director of the center.

Third Party: Gu Zhangze, male, born on March 28, 1964, Han Chinese, residing in Zhenjiang City, Jiangsu Province.

The plaintiff, Zhenjiang Hongxing Magnetic Separation Equipment Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hongxing Company), filed a lawsuit with the Runzhou District People's Court of Zhenjiang City, Jiangsu Province, against the defendant, Zhenjiang Housing Provident Fund Management Center (hereinafter referred to as the Provident Fund Center), and the third party, Gu Zhangze, concerning a dispute over an administrative handling decision on the contribution of housing provident funds.

Plaintiff's Allegations: The third party, Gu Zhangze, was originally a salesperson for the plaintiff. On January 14, 2016, the third party issued a letter of undertaking to the plaintiff stating that the financial matters between the parties had been fully settled. On January 19, 2016, the third party and the plaintiff terminated the labor relationship by mutual agreement. A civil judgment of the Runzhou District People's Court of Zhenjiang City, Jiangsu Province, which has become effective, confirmed that the termination of labor relations by agreement between the third party and the plaintiff was lawful and valid. In April 2016, the third party filed a complaint with the defendant, the Provident Fund Center, requesting the plaintiff to pay housing provident funds. On July 4, 2016, the defendant issued Administrative Handling Decision No. [2016] 4, ordering the plaintiff to make retroactive contributions of housing provident funds. The plaintiff argued that the defendant's administrative handling decision lacked factual and legal basis and, therefore, petitioned the court to revoke the defendant's Administrative Handling Decision No. [2016] 4.

Defendant's Defense: 1. The defendant has the administrative authority to handle matters concerning the non-payment of housing provident funds by units. 2. The specific administrative act undertaken by the defendant was lawful. 3. The specific administrative act undertaken by the defendant did not infringe upon the effective civil judgment (judicial power). In summary, the defendant requested that the court reject the plaintiff's claims.

Third Party's Statement: The third party argued that there was no written agreement proving that an understanding had been reached with the plaintiff, Hongxing Company, and that the letter of undertaking did not reflect his true intention. He requested that the plaintiff's claims be rejected.

Facts Found by the Court at First Instance (Runzhou District People's Court of Zhenjiang City):

The third party, Gu Zhangze, was originally a salesperson for the plaintiff, Hongxing Company. On January 14, 2016, the third party issued a letter of undertaking to the plaintiff stating: "Financially settled with the company." On January 19 of the same year, the plaintiff issued a certificate of termination and rescission of the labor contract to the third party and processed the job resignation registration. In April 2016, the third party submitted a "Claim for Recovery of Housing Provident Fund" to the defendant, the Provident Fund Center, requesting that the defendant recover from the plaintiff the housing provident funds and late fees due to the third party for the period of the existing labor relationship from September 2011 to January 2016 (a total of 53 months). The defendant ascertained that during the existence of the labor relationship between the plaintiff and the third party, the plaintiff had indeed not contributed housing provident funds for the third party. Therefore, on July 4, 2016, the defendant issued Administrative Handling Decision No. [2016] 4, ordering the plaintiff to retroactively contribute the unpaid housing provident funds for the third party for the period of the existing labor relationship from September 2011 to January 2016, totaling RMB 6,913, and ordering the third party to contribute a corresponding amount of RMB 6,913.

It was further found that on March 2016, the third party, Gu Zhangze, filed a lawsuit against the plaintiff, Hongxing Company, with the Runzhou District People's Court of Zhenjiang City, Jiangsu Province, requesting that the plaintiff make up for the wage difference and pay economic compensation. The Runzhou District People's Court issued a first-instance judgment on June 6, 2016, which confirmed that the termination of labor relations by agreement between the third party and the plaintiff on January 2016 was lawful and valid. That judgment has become effective. The defendant, the Provident Fund Center, was aware of this before making the administrative handling decision.

Opinion of the Court at First Instance (Runzhou District People's Court of Zhenjiang City):

The Court considered that Article 1 of the "Regulations on the Administration of Housing Provident Funds" states: "These Regulations are formulated to strengthen the management of housing provident funds, safeguard the legitimate rights and interests of housing provident fund owners, promote urban housing construction, and improve the living standards of urban residents." Article 3 states: "The housing provident funds contributed by individual employees and the housing provident funds contributed by the unit where the employee works belong to the individual employee." From the above provisions, it can be seen that housing provident funds are personal rights and interests of the employee, and one of the purposes of the "Regulations on the Administration of Housing Provident Funds" is to protect the legitimate rights and interests of employees. Since housing provident funds belong to the personal rights and interests of employees, employees have the right to dispose of them. In this case, when the third party, Gu Zhangze, negotiated the termination of the labor relationship with the plaintiff, Hongxing Company, he issued a letter of undertaking stating "financially settled with the company." There is no evidence to show that this undertaking was not the true intention of the third party. It should be regarded that the third party had disposed of the economic interests related to himself and the plaintiff and could no longer claim rights from the plaintiff. Specifically in this case, it means that the third party, when terminating the labor relationship by agreement with the plaintiff, had waived the right to request the plaintiff to contribute housing provident funds for him. "Where there is a right, there is a remedy." Since the right has been waived, there is no need for a remedy. Therefore, the subsequent intervention of the defendant, the Provident Fund Center, lacked a prerequisite, and the administrative handling decision it made had no legal or regulatory basis and should be revoked. The plaintiff's claim was established and should be supported.

Accordingly, the Runzhou District People's Court of Zhenjiang City, Jiangsu Province, rendered judgment on May 26, 2017, in accordance with Article 70, Item (2) of the "Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China":

Revoke the defendant Zhenjiang Housing Provident Fund Management Center's Administrative Handling Decision No. [2016] 4.

The Provident Fund Center was dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment and appealed to the Zhenjiang Intermediate People's Court, Jiangsu Province, on the following grounds: 1. The subjects of the legal obligation to contribute housing provident funds include both units and employees; the employee's contribution obligation is fulfilled through the unit's withholding and contribution. The Housing Provident Fund Management Center, as an institution authorized by law and regulations, has the authority to handle cases of non-contribution or under-contribution in accordance with the law. As a subject of obligation, an employee does not have the right to choose to waive the legal obligation to contribute housing provident funds. 2. The "Regulations on the Administration of Housing Provident Funds" clearly stipulate that units shall contribute housing provident funds in full and on time, and must not delay or under-contribute. The obligation for units and employees to contribute housing provident funds in full and on time is mandatory. Even if a unit and an employee negotiate and agree not to contribute, to under-contribute, or to contribute not on time, such an agreement is invalid because it violates mandatory provisions of laws and regulations. 3. Housing provident funds refer to long-term housing reserves contributed by state organs, state-owned enterprises, urban collective enterprises, foreign-invested enterprises, urban private enterprises, and other urban enterprises, public institutions, private non-enterprise units, social organizations, and their current employees. The first-instance court's view that housing provident funds belong to the personal rights and interests of employees and that employees therefore have the right to dispose of them is erroneous. In summary, the first-instance judgment applied the law incorrectly. The appellant requested that the first-instance judgment be revoked and a new judgment be rendered in accordance with law.

The respondent, Hongxing Company, argued: As the employer, the respondent had fulfilled its due obligations. The third party at first instance, Gu Zhangze, voluntarily waived his rights. On January 19, 2016, through a meeting and written minutes, the respondent had clearly explained the situation to the third party, who made a clear statement and wrote the letter of undertaking after receiving compensation. The third party voluntarily waived his rights. The respondent requested that the appeal be dismissed and the first-instance judgment be upheld.

The third party at first instance, Gu Zhangze, stated: He supported the appellant, the Provident Fund Center's, appeal request, asked that the lawful rights and interests of the third party be protected, that social fairness and the legitimate rights and interests of employees be upheld, and that the respondent Hongxing Company's malicious evasion of all interests related to employee remuneration under labor law be corrected.

The Zhenjiang Intermediate People's Court, Jiangsu Province, confirmed the facts found at first instance upon second-instance review.

It was further found: The labor dispute case brought by the third party at first instance, Gu Zhangze, against the respondent, Hongxing Company, was filed for arbitration with the Zhenjiang Labor and Personnel Dispute Arbitration Commission on January 26, 2016. The Arbitration Commission issued Arbitration Decision No. [2016] 52, which stated: Gu Zhangze explicitly promised "financially settled with the company." In the absence of evidence that the promise was invalid or subject to revocation, the validity of the promise was recognized. This written promise was essentially an effective disposition by Gu Zhangze of his relevant rights regarding "financial" matters. In labor legal relations, such "financial" rights should include wages, economic compensation, and the like. The arbitration decision confirmed the existence of a labor relationship between Gu Zhangze and Hongxing Company from September 2011 to January 2016 and ordered Hongxing Company to pay Gu Zhangze an economic compensation difference of RMB 3,000. In March 2016, Gu Zhangze filed a civil lawsuit with the first-instance court, requesting Hongxing Company to make up the wage difference and pay economic compensation, among other things. On June 6, 2016, the first-instance court issued effective judgment (2016) Su 1111 Min Chu No. 973, confirming that the termination of labor relations by agreement between Gu Zhangze and Hongxing Company on January 2016 was lawful and valid; ordering Hongxing Company to pay Gu Zhangze a business fee of RMB 2,378; ordering Hongxing Company to deliver the original of the sales agreement for the Jiangsu Mengjiagang project or a verified copy thereof; and dismissing Gu Zhangze's other claims.

Opinion of the Zhenjiang Intermediate People's Court on Second Instance:

The Court held that housing provident funds are long-term housing reserves contributed by state organs, state-owned enterprises, urban collective enterprises, foreign-invested enterprises, urban private enterprises, and other urban enterprises, public institutions, private non-enterprise units, social organizations, and their current employees. The "Regulations on the Administration of Housing Provident Funds" (hereinafter referred to as the "Regulations") clearly specify the scope, subjects, amounts, methods, time limits for contributions, as well as the withdrawal, use, management, and supervision of housing provident funds. Article 13 of the Regulations provides that housing provident fund management centers shall set up dedicated housing provident fund accounts at entrusted banks. Units shall register with the housing provident fund management center for housing provident fund contributions and establish housing provident fund accounts for their employees. Each employee can only have one housing provident fund account. Article 19 provides that the housing provident fund contributed by an individual employee shall be withheld from their monthly wages by their unit. The unit shall, within five days from the date of paying the employee's wages each month, remit the unit's contribution and the withheld employee's contribution to the dedicated housing provident fund account, which shall be recorded by the entrusted bank into the employee's housing provident fund account. Article 20, Paragraph 1, provides that units shall contribute housing provident funds on time and in full, and must not delay or under-contribute. Article 38 provides that if a unit violates the provisions of these Regulations by delaying or under-contributing housing provident funds, the housing provident fund management center shall order the unit to make the contribution within a specified period; if the unit still fails to contribute within the specified period, the center may apply to the People's Court for compulsory enforcement. It follows that the state implements a compulsory savings and dedicated account storage system for housing provident funds. The housing provident funds contributed by the employer for the employee shall be contributed in accordance with the law into the employee's housing provident fund account. If the employer delays or under-contributes housing provident funds, the housing provident fund management center may order the contribution to be made within a specified period.

Contributing housing provident funds for employees by the employer is its statutory obligation. The amount and method of contribution are also mandatory legal provisions. Therefore, the employer and employee may not change the contribution method or reduce the contribution obligation through negotiation. In this case, neither the Arbitration Decision No. [2016] 52 of the Zhenjiang Labor and Personnel Dispute Arbitration Commission nor the civil judgment (2016) Su 1111 Min Chu No. 973 determined that the phrase "financially settled with the company" included the housing provident fund contributions that should have been made. Moreover, regardless of whether the third party at first instance, Gu Zhangze's, promise of "financially settled with the company" included an agreement on provident funds, it cannot exempt the respondent, Hongxing Company, from its statutory obligation to contribute housing provident funds in the statutory manner and amount in a timely manner for the original third party at first instance, Gu Zhangze. Hongxing Company's defense that it had reached an agreement with the third party at first instance upon termination of the labor relationship and was no longer subject to any statutory obligations was untenable.

Upon receiving the complaint from the third party at first instance, Gu Zhangze, the appellant, the Provident Fund Center, conducted an investigation and determined that during Gu Zhangze's tenure, the respondent, Hongxing Company, had not contributed housing provident funds in full and on time for him. The Center then calculated, based on the annual housing provident fund contribution ratio, the amount of retroactive contributions that Hongxing Company should make and informed Hongxing Company of the facts, reasons, and legal basis for the proposed administrative handling decision ordering the retroactive contribution within a specified period. Subsequently, the Center issued Administrative Handling Decision No. [2016] 4, ordering Hongxing Company and Gu Zhangze to each retroactively contribute RMB 6,913 in housing provident funds, and served the decision on all relevant parties. The administrative handling decision made by the Provident Fund Center was based on clear facts, was procedurally lawful, and applied the law correctly. The first-instance judgment revoking the Provident Fund Center's Administrative Handling Decision No. [2016] 4 wrongly applied the law and should be corrected.

In conclusion, the Zhenjiang Intermediate People's Court, Jiangsu Province, rendered judgment on October 11, 2017, in accordance with Article 89, Paragraph 1, Item (2), and Paragraph 3 of the "Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China":

I. Revoke the administrative judgment (2017) Su 1111 Xing Chu No. 1 of the Runzhou District People's Court of Zhenjiang City, Jiangsu Province;
II. Dismiss Hongxing Company's claim requesting the revocation of the Administrative Handling Decision No. [2016] 4 of Zhenjiang Housing Provident Fund Management Center.

This judgment is final.
